Essentials 2.0 · Flow inspiration · 05-inventory

Inventory: ideas from other products

This page shows examples from other products for the Inventory module of Essentials 2.0, grouped by product. They cover tracking sim-center equipment and consumables (manikins, task trainers, monitors, IV kits, moulage), check-in and check-out, low-stock alerts, and AI analysis of a scenario equipment list. Adding equipment to a scenario belongs to Scenario manager. Room booking belongs to Scheduling. Sources: the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero, researched on 30 September 2026. Refero returned no usable flows, because the images of its one match would not load.

What we have today. Essentials has no inventory today. LearningSpace Enterprise has an Inventory Manager dashboard module. Inventory was dropped on 10 September 2026 and brought back on 18 September as an optional paid add-on, because small centers stayed on Enterprise for it. The direction is light and predictive rather than counting gloves and needles. That means automatic check-in and check-out from scenario runs, trend and reorder notices, equipment scheduling, and a usage report. Failure cases (shortage, two scenarios needing the same item at once, returns, manual correction) are still undefined.

How to read this page

Each section below is one product. Each strip of screenshots is one flow: a real sequence of screens, in the order a user sees them. Click a screenshot to enlarge it. "Worth borrowing" lists ideas we could use, and "Avoid" lists what we should not copy. Use the task filters to see only one task, and click ☆ on a flow to add it to your own shortlist.

What the best products have in common

  1. Pick the kind of thing, then a short form Square starts 'Create item' with an item-type chooser, then buries the user in retail fields (channels, taxes, nutrition, two prices), which makes it the example of what not to do. Fresha's form is shorter and adds what consumables need: a measure with an amount, and a switch that removes selling fields. Deel's device form asks only model and serial (required), condition and notes. For Essentials, choosing the type first (equipment or consumable) should decide whether the form asks for serial number and condition, or unit and quantity.See: Square: Creating an item (manually) · Fresha: Adding a product · Deel: Adding equipment
  2. Track where equipment is, count only consumables Deel's asset list opens on a location-status bar (With worker, In transit, In storage, Write off) instead of quantities. An assigned device sits in Pending shipping until someone marks it delivered. Square's list shows a quantity label ('20 available') per item. The two models fit 'light, not counting gloves': status for durable gear like manikins, quantity only for consumables.See: Deel: Asset detail · Deel: Adding equipment · Square: Creating an item (manually)
  3. Import is review-first, with an explicit merge rule and an error report Square's empty library offers Create, Import and Download template side by side. The import lands in an editable grid, asks 'Add and update existing' or 'Delete and overwrite', and on failure shows counts with a downloadable error report and 'Upload fixed errors'. Before any products exist, Fresha's screen offers import and low-stock reminders together. This matches what the Scheduling report found in Attio, and fits centers moving a spreadsheet off Enterprise.See: Square: Importing items · Fresha: Adding a product
  4. The alert level is set on the item, and the alert says where it will appear Square sets the low-stock amount per location from the 'more' menu on the list row, without opening the full edit form. Its wording says where the alert appears: a low-stock mark in the library plus a daily email digest. Kitchen Stories turns shortage into a headline ('14 out of 14 items missing') before the list opens. Neither shows the next step, a reorder or purchase request.See: Square: Updating low stock alert · Kitchen Stories: Shopping list
  5. Scan, confirm, stay in the camera Luma identifies the scanned record on a sliding panel and changes only when the user taps 'Check In'. Then it keeps the camera live with a success message strip and Undo. Woolworths keeps a running tally and item count, offers a keypad for unreadable barcodes, and ends on an itemized, timestamped receipt. Both put a manual fallback next to the camera, which a sim tech with a scuffed label will need.See: Luma: Checking in a guest · Woolworths: Purchasing a product (Scan & Go)
  6. Returns end with evidence and a timestamp Turo's return starts from a countdown screen with 'Report damage', walks through condition photos from both parties, and requires liability agreement before 'Finish checkout' records the end time. Woolworths closes with a receipt. Deel captures condition at intake. Turo asks for about 23 photos. Essentials should ask for condition evidence only on high-value items such as simulators.See: Turo: Ending a trip · Woolworths: Purchasing a product (Scan & Go) · Deel: Adding equipment
  7. AI extraction shows the source and asks for a match per line Airwallex's bill flow puts the uploaded PDF beside the extracted form. Each parsed line has 'Match with PO' to link it to an existing purchase order (PO). Its receipt flow keeps uploading without blocking ('upload more while they match'), shows a 'Matching…' wait, then a review card with Skip and Delete for wrong results. Kitchen Stories is the manual counterpart: the list comes from the recipe, but pantry matching is ticking by hand. Together they suggest this: the scenario list goes in, each item gets a row marked matched, unmatched or short, and then a person confirms.See: Airwallex: Adding a bill · Airwallex: Uploading a receipt · Kitchen Stories: Shopping list
  8. Block the asset, not the person Turo's availability screen separates host hours from the vehicle calendar, with a nudge to 'block the asset itself', and blocks a start and end window in one Add. That is the only flow here that prevents two bookings claiming the same item. Kitchen Stories' servings control is the demand side: quantity scales with people, like consumables with learner count.See: Turo: Blocking availability · Kitchen Stories: Shopping list

Questions we still need to answer

  • No reorder, purchase-order or purchase-request flow is in the report. Refero had Shopify 'Create and place purchase order' (14 steps), but none of its images would load, and Mobbin returned nothing usable for Ramp/Brex purchase requests. Where does a low-stock alert go next in a sim center: an email to a purchaser, a request inside Essentials, or the hospital's procurement system?
  • No dedicated equipment-inventory tool (Sortly, Cheqroom, Snipe-IT, EZOfficeInventory, Asset Panda, itemit, Shelf.nu) appears on Mobbin or Refero. Deel is the closest match, but its inventory is tied to hiring, so stock and check-out models here are borrowed from retail, rentals and events. Compare against LearningSpace Enterprise's Inventory Manager before deciding what to keep.
  • Auto check-in and check-out driven by scenario runs has no direct evidence: every automatic flow here (Luma, Woolworths) is triggered by a scan. What should subtract used items in Essentials: session start, session end confirmed by the sim tech, or the booking itself? And how is a mistake corrected? Luma's Undo is the only correction shown.
  • Two scenarios needing the same item at the same time: only Turo's block window touches this, and it prevents rather than warns. Scheduling found conflicts are best counted and graded, not blocked. Which applies to equipment, and does it show in the scenario, the booking or inventory?
  • No flow shows returning a partial quantity, an overdue case, or reconciling consumables used versus returned. Kitchen Stories scales demand with a servings control. Should consumable demand scale with learner count per session?
  • How much evidence should a return require? Turo's two-party photo set suits a car. For a sim center, it may apply only to high-value simulators, with consumables closed by a Woolworths-style tally.

Square

Same task, different field3 flows

Square covers the full retail stock cycle. Its CSV import lets you review before saving, choose whether to merge or overwrite, and get an error report. A low-stock level set from the list feeds both a mark in the library and a daily email. Its item form is so heavy that it is this page's example of what not to do.

WebMobbin12 steps

Importing items

From an empty Item library the user uploads a CSV, reviews an editable grid, chooses add-and-update vs overwrite, hits an all-failed error with a downloadable report, then sees 'Import Successful'.

Basic inventory items

Worth borrowing

  • Before any items exist, dual path: Create an item, Import items, and Download template (screen 1).
  • An editable review grid before commit, with row delete (screens 5–6).
  • An explicit merge decision: 'Add and update existing' vs 'Delete and overwrite' (screen 7).
  • Failure pop-up: Require review vs Imported successfully counts, plus Download error report and Upload fixed errors (screen 9).

Avoid

  • A blocking full-page import that warns 'don't leave this page' (screen 4) when a later step already allows closing and continuing elsewhere (screen 8).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: extends item first-time setup for centers migrating catalogs. Merge vs overwrite and the error-report loop help where failure cases are still undefined.

WebMobbin4 steps

Updating low stock alert

From Item library row actions the user opens 'Update low stock alert', sets amount and location, updates, and gets a short success message without leaving the list.

Low quantity alert

Worth borrowing

  • Low-stock settings are reachable from the list row more menu without opening full edit (screen 1).
  • Wording that names both places the alert appears: marked low stock in the library and a daily low stock alert email (screens 2–3).
  • Alert amount and Locations are set together (screen 3).
  • A stay-on-list success message after the threshold saves (screen 4).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: extends planned reorder and trend notifications: per-item threshold plus location plus digest email maps cleanly. Skip retail-only list extras.

Creating an item (manually)

From Square home the user opens 'Create item', picks a type, fills a dense point-of-sale (POS) form, saves, and lands on Item library with a short created message.

Basic inventory items

Worth borrowing

  • An item-type chooser comes first so later fields match the kind of thing, which maps to Equipment vs Consumable vs Service (screen 2).
  • Internal name and customer-facing name sit on one form (screens 4–5).
  • Status, Categories, and Locations sit in a side menu beside the main form (screens 3–11).
  • A list status label with quantity (for example '20 available') plus a created message (screen 12).

Avoid

  • Kitchen name, menus, sales channels, taxes, nutritional accordion, and dual retail or online prices are retail POS fields that fight a light sim-center catalog.

What it means for Essentials Inventory: example of what not to do for Essentials' light inventory. Replace with a short type, then name, unit, location, and photo create. Keep type-first and location side-menu ideas only.

Deel

Close match2 flows

Deel tracks equipment by where it is, not by how many there are. The overview shows 'With worker', 'In transit', 'In storage' and 'Write off', an assigned device shows 'Pending shipping', and a quick view separates tracking from asset details.

WebMobbin3 steps

Asset detail

Assets list with a location-status overview opens a ThinkPad quick view: Tracking (In storage, intake date, no service) then Asset details (IDs, condition, purchase and end-of-life).

Basic inventory items

Worth borrowing

  • The location overview bar shows With worker / In transit / In storage / Write off counts across total inventory (screen 1).
  • List actions include 'Bulk import' and Add asset, filters for Worker, storage locations, and Category, and Quick view per row (screen 1).
  • The Tracking tab shows location label In storage, named storage site, Storage intake date, and empty service offers send to storage, assign, or retire (screen 2).
  • Asset details show Asset ID and Serial you can duplicate to the clipboard, Condition, Purchase date, and End of life date even when Not specified (screen 3).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: strong items pattern for an asset registry: status distribution, quick panel with tracking versus identity, and lifecycle dates. Lighter than Enterprise counting, richer than a flat list.

WebMobbin6 steps

Adding equipment

From the hiring Benefits step, admin opens Equipment, adds a device (type, model, serial, condition, notes) when inventory is empty, and ends with the laptop assigned and status Pending shipping.

Basic inventory itemsManual check in and check out

Worth borrowing

  • When nothing can be assigned, the screen says 'There are no devices to be assigned from your inventory' and 'Add New' is the only way forward (screen 3).
  • The device form requires Model and Serial/Unique ID with character limits, makes Condition optional, and notes 'These notes are shared with your worker.' (screen 5).
  • After assign, the item card shows type, model, and serial, Status = Pending shipping, and that shipping is marked later from the device overview (screen 6).
  • Continue stays disabled until a device is selected (screen 3).

Avoid

  • Full item creation sits inside an unrelated multi-step hire form; create and assign should be reachable from Assets itself, not only during first-time setup.

What it means for Essentials Inventory: extends items and manual check-out with typed assets that have serial and condition, assign-to-person, and a logistics status for out for delivery between storage and borrower.

Turo

Outside idea2 flows

Turo shows how to lend an expensive asset. A return starts from a countdown, both parties take condition photos, and they confirm liability before the end time is recorded. It also blocks the asset itself, not the person, for a date range.

iOSMobbin8 steps

Ending a trip

Guest opens 'End trip' with time remaining, documents with photos, reviews host and guest sets, accepts liability on 'Finish checkout', and lands on trip-ended with a timestamp.

Manual check in and check out

Worth borrowing

  • The pre-return screen shows a countdown ('ends in 2h 30m'), Change trip, Report damage, and End trip that needs a short inspection before checkout (screen 1).
  • Photo guidance shows a recommended area count, 'View all exterior areas', a why-it-matters callout, Take photos vs Upload from Photos, and Skip allowed (screens 2–3).
  • A shared photo log sections by party (host vs guest) with per-photo timestamps before Continue (screen 5).
  • 'Finish checkout' requires agreeing the inspection is accurate and you are liable for unreported damage, then Submit shows Trip ended time and notifies the other party (screen 7).

Avoid

  • Requiring about 15 exterior plus about 8 interior photos for every sim-equipment return. Scale documentation to high-value assets only.

What it means for Essentials Inventory: fills the undefined return and damage path for manual check-out: condition photos, evidence from both parties, liability confirm, and an explicit return time before the item is free again.

iOSMobbin6 steps

Blocking availability

From Pickup and return hours, host opens 'Block availability' (empty), sets start and end date-time with calendar and time wheels, and confirms Add for a blocked window.

Manual check in and check out

Worth borrowing

  • When nothing is blocked, 'No hours blocked' and 'Block availability' appear, noting host unavailability is not vehicle unavailability, with 'Go to Calendar' to block the asset itself (screen 2).
  • The block form has Start and End date plus time, a month calendar on the form, a 30-minute time drum, and a single Add to commit (screens 3–6).
  • Always available and per-weekday Available hours sit beside Block availability for one-off windows (screen 1).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: maps to equipment scheduling and conflict handling: block a manikin or room for maintenance or exclusive use so two scenarios cannot claim the same asset. Keep the job as check-out-manual among current ids.

Woolworths

Same task, different field1 flow

Woolworths' Scan & Go treats shopping as a session. Each scan adds to a running total; a keypad works when a barcode won't scan, you finish at the physical checkout, and an itemized, timestamped receipt is the audit trail.

iOSMobbin9 steps

Purchasing a product (Scan & Go)

From In-store home, user starts Scan&Go, scans into a running tally, reviews My Items, is sent to physical checkout with a pending QR, and finishes on a dated receipt.

Automated check in and check out

Worth borrowing

  • During the session, a live dollar total and N Items tally, Scan an item as the main action, and keypad or manual barcode fallback beside dismiss (screens 3–4).
  • After a scan, My Items offers Continue to Payment, Scan next item, or Use my lists, so you can keep scanning or finalize (screen 5).
  • An information strip forces Pay at Scan&Go Checkout; Payment Pending shows a kiosk QR plus I've scanned my code (screens 7–8).
  • Closure is a receipt with itemized list, store, POS, and transaction ids, plus a timestamp as the audit trail after auto checkout (screen 9).

Avoid

  • Retail payment and rewards steps (Adding Rewards, Visa checkout). Essentials needs session or room assignment, not purchase.

What it means for Essentials Inventory: strong automated check-out analog for barcode check-out of kits or consumables: scan loop, running count, optional list attach, then physical confirm via QR and a durable usage receipt.

Luma

Outside idea1 flow

Luma has the tightest scan loop: scan, confirm on a panel that slides up, see success with 'Undo', and the camera stays on. A list icon is the fallback when a code won't scan.

iOSMobbin6 steps

Checking in a guest

From event details the host taps 'Check In Guests', opens the QR camera, confirms the guest on a sliding panel, sees success with Undo, then scans the next guest.

Automated check in and check out

Worth borrowing

  • Scan, identify on a panel, then an explicit 'Check In' confirms before anything changes, which maps to equipment check-out (screens 2–3).
  • A list icon beside the camera is the manual fallback when the code will not scan (screens 2, 6).
  • A green 'Check In Successful' message keeps the camera live for continuous scan (screens 4–5).
  • 'Undo Check In' with Registered and Checked In times corrects a wrong scan or already-in case right away (screen 5).

Avoid

  • This flow has no unrecognized-code or already-checked-in error panel, only the normal case plus Undo after success (screens 2–6).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: extends automated check-out: host QR scan stands in for barcode or NFC on a kit, identify, confirm, then success; Undo covers mis-scan; list fallback covers failed scan.

Airwallex

Same task, different field2 flows

Airwallex's AI extraction shows its work. The source document sits beside the form it filled in, each line has 'Match with PO', a 'Matching…' wait doesn't block you, and wrong matches can be skipped or deleted.

WebMobbin9 steps

Adding a bill

From empty Bills the user opens 'Add new bill', drops an invoice, waits through 'Extracting bill details', edits lines with 'Match with PO', comments, submits, and lands on statused Bills.

AI analyses the equipment list

Worth borrowing

  • Source PDF on the left and structured form on the right lets you verify the extract while editing (screens 5–8).
  • The 'Extracting…' pop-up says 'up to a minute', so the AI wait is honest without freezing the form (screen 4).
  • 'Match with PO' on each extracted line links parsed text to an existing catalog or purchase order (screens 6–7).
  • Draft, Pending approval, and Overdue on the table after submit show the lifecycle after an AI create (screen 9).

Avoid

  • The marketing Spend home and accounting-connect promos add noise before the extract and match work (screen 1).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: nearby pattern for AI equipment analysis: upload a scenario list, extract lines, match each to the shelf or catalog, then save a draft or flag gaps. Overdue also models late returns.

iOSMobbin6 steps

Uploading a receipt

From Spend reimbursements the user opens 'Upload receipts', watches upload then AI matching, reviews vendor and amount, and chooses 'Card expense' or 'Reimbursement' (or Delete or Skip).

AI analyses the equipment list

Worth borrowing

  • While Uploading and Matching, the screen says you can 'upload more while they match', so a batch can keep going (screens 3–4).
  • A 'Matching…' sparkle on the file row makes the AI wait visible before results (screen 4).
  • A ready-to-review card shows vendor, date, amount, and thumbnail so you can glance-check automatic text reading from a photo or scan (OCR) before deep edit (screen 5).
  • The match panel offers primary and secondary destinations plus Delete and Skip for unmatched or wrong extracts (screen 6).

Avoid

  • The 'Card expense' vs 'Reimbursement' fork is spend-ledger routing; inventory needs match-to-shelf, create-item, or flag-shortage, not payment buckets (screen 6).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: maps to AI equipment analysis as upload a list, extract with AI, review, then match or route unmatched rows; receipt-to-expense becomes list-to-shelf match and shortages.

Kitchen Stories

Outside idea1 flow

Kitchen Stories turns a recipe into a shortage list: 'N out of N missing', a servings control that scales quantities, and ticks for items already in the pantry. It is a manual version of checking a scenario's list against the shelf.

iOSMobbin6 steps

Shopping list

From Home, the user opens an empty shopping list, adds recipes, checks how many items are missing, scales the servings, and ticks off what they already have.

AI analyses the equipment listLow quantity alert

Worth borrowing

  • Each recipe shows a shortage headline such as '14 out of 14 items missing' before you open its list (screen 3).
  • Tabs switch between a list per recipe and one combined list, like grouping by scenario or flattening for a prep run (screens 3 to 6).
  • A servings control scales the quantities, like multiplying consumables by the number of learners or repeat runs (screen 4).
  • Ticking an item strikes it through, and 'Unmark all' resets the list for the next session (screens 5 to 6).

Avoid

  • Matching is by hand only, with no automatic check against what is on the shelf, while the baseline asks for AI or shelf matching (screens 4 to 6).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: a manual model for the AI equipment check. A recipe is like a scenario's equipment list, missing items are gaps on the shelf, and ticked items are already there. It does not subtract stock automatically.

Fresha

Same task, different field1 flow

Fresha's item form is lighter than Square's. It has a measure plus amount for consumables (ml 100), a barcode warning that doesn't block saving, and a retail switch that hides selling fields for stock-only items.

WebMobbin12 steps

Adding a product

From empty Products the user starts 'Add new product', fills name, barcode, brand, measure, descriptions, photo, category, Pricing and Inventory (stock code / SKU), saves, and lands on Product list.

Basic inventory items

Worth borrowing

  • Before any products exist, one pitch offers 'Start now', import many at once, and low stock reminders together (screen 1).
  • Barcode validation warns without blocking save (screens 3–9).
  • A measure list paired with Amount (ml 100) fits volume consumables (screens 4–5).
  • An 'Enable retail sales' switch can hide sell and commission fields when the item is stock-only (screen 10).

Avoid

  • Team member commission plus markup and tax on create are salon POS fields, not sim equipment (screens 10–11).

What it means for Essentials Inventory: extends basic items with barcode plus unit and amount for consumables and later scan check-out; clash if we ship full retail pricing on create. Splitting Catalog from Inventory (Stocktakes / Stock orders / Suppliers) is a useful structure hint.
